sections.html:
Two offices share the work in Ben Hill County. The Tax Commissioner at 324 East Pine Street in Fitzgerald sends bills and takes payments, and the Board of Tax Assessors decides what a property is worth. Call the commissioner at (229) 426-5144 on weekdays, with the counter staffed until half past four. The assessors answer at (229) 426-5147.

Take payments, liens and mailing address problems to the commissioner. Take value, homestead and exemption questions to the assessors. Appraisers inspect properties on an ongoing basis, visit every parcel with a building permit, and check mobile homes for a current decal.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, receipts, liens, online payments
  • Board of Tax Assessors: value, returns, exemptions, notices of assessment
  • Clerk of Superior Court: copies of your warranty deed, kept in the deed room at the courthouse

sections.h2: Ben Hill County at a glance
sections.html:
Ben Hill is a small south Georgia county, and Fitzgerald is both its only city and its seat. The population slipped from 17,194 at the 2020 census to an estimate of 17,099 for 2025. The middle home value is $112,700 against a middle household income of $41,758, so a tax bill weighs more on an owner here than it would in a pricier market.

The county has 8,166 housing units in 2025 and a 63.3 percent owner rate. Middle gross rent is $688 a month and the average commute is only 16.8 minutes. Buyers in this price range tend to be careful with money, which is a reason to clear any tax question before you list.

December 1 is the usual due date for land, houses and business personal property. Georgia's default is December 20 and counties may move it, so go by the day printed on your own statement. The mobile home date is April 1, but ask the office to confirm it for your account.

Late accounts accrue interest of 1% a month. A one-time 10% penalty applies once 90 days pass, except that a homesteaded parcel owing under $500 escapes that penalty. A balance older than 90 days can also become a FiFa lien in the Clerk of Superior Court's records, where credit bureaus may see it, and the commissioner is then free to levy on the parcel.

Statements go to the owner, not the lender. With an escrow account, pass the bill along or check that the servicer is paying it.

Cash and checks at the counter cost nothing extra, and a mailed check works as well. Online payment runs through the county's GovtWindow portal, with PayPal and cards offered only on the website. Each online method adds a convenience charge that appears before you confirm, so you can stop and pay by check instead.

  • In person: 324 East Pine Street, Fitzgerald, Georgia 31750
  • By phone for questions: (229) 426-5144
  • Portal help line: (877) 575-7233

Owning and living in the house on January 1 is the test, and the application has to land at the assessors' office ahead of April 1. A filing carries forward each year while you stay put. If you move, you reapply for the new address, and a late filing simply pushes the benefit to the next tax year.

Homeowners who reach age 62 can apply for an additional exemption. Business inventory can qualify for a freeport exemption where local voters have approved one. For the dollar amount on your own bill, call the assessors, since local legislation can increase the base amounts.

sections.h2: How values are set and challenged
sections.html:
Each winter and early spring, up to the first of April, an owner may file a return naming a value. If the board disagrees it mails a notice with its figure. Taxable value is 40% of market value, and every mill raises one dollar for each $1,000 of that taxable value.

The clock for an appeal is 45 days from the notice date, and the appeal goes to the county Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. If you are unhappy with that result, you can continue in superior court by delivering written notice to the assessors. Refund requests for tax charged in error have a three-year limit, counted from payment.

Learn the balance and the billed owner before you sign. Because the January 1 owner is on the statement, it can carry your name even when the buyer takes the deed later in the year. Ask the commissioner for a printed balance, and ask whoever runs the closing how that year is shared with the buyer.

A recorded lien must be cleared before clean title can pass. Most sellers settle it out of the sale money, and the commissioner's payoff number is the amount to wire. Needed repairs do not stop a sale while taxes are owed, which is one reason some owners choose a cash buyer who takes the house as it is.

Bring your deed or parcel number, your latest statement and any lien notice to the counter at 324 East Pine Street. Ask for the payoff in writing and note the date it is good through, since interest builds each month.

Mobile and modular homes count as personal property in Georgia, so the owner files a return and obtains a location permit each year. The current year's mobile home tax must be paid in full before the permit is issued, and April 1 is the due date for that account. A call to the commissioner is worth making to confirm the date on yours.

The assessors also check mobile homes for a current decal during their inspections. Selling one means the next owner inherits the paperwork trail, so settle the year's tax and the permit before you hand over the home. Keep the paid receipt, since the permit cannot be issued until the tax is paid.

The assessors also keep a 2026 meeting calendar for the Board of Assessors, a 2026 deadlines sheet and a returned mail listing. Owners who moved and never updated an address should check that list so notices reach them.

faqs.q: When is real estate tax due in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: December 1 is the usual date, and the date printed on your statement controls. The office at (229) 426-5144 can confirm.

faqs.q: What does a late Ben Hill County payment cost?
faqs.a: Expect 1% interest per month, plus a 10% penalty once 90 days have gone by. Homesteaded property with a liability under $500 skips the penalty.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for homestead exemption in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: File with the Tax Assessor so the paperwork arrives ahead of April 1. Ownership and residence on January 1 are both required.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date on the assessment notice. The appeal goes to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and superior court is the next step.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Ben Hill County taxes without a fee?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash or a check at 324 East Pine Street, or a mailed check, has no fee, while online payments carry a convenience charge.
